prompt:
Night, torrential rain, a crowded wet Bengaluru street in 2047.

A BUSY PAVEMENT SEEN STRAIGHT ON. Fifteen or twenty ordinary Indian people of all ages, soaked
through, moving past camera under a concrete awning — hurrying, sheltering, carrying bags,
heads down against the rain. Everyone is wet, tired, unremarkable and unaware of the camera.

ONE FIGURE IN THE MIDDLE OF THEM IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL AND LOOKING DIRECTLY AT CAMERA.

A man in his thirties in plain ordinary clothing. Entirely unremarkable. Not menacing, not
posed, not lit differently, not centred, not larger. AT A GLANCE HE IS JUST ANOTHER PERSON IN
THE CROWD. He is not a robot to look at — normal human skin, a normal human face.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG AND NONE OF THEM IS OBVIOUS:

HE IS COMPLETELY DRY. His hair, his face and his clothing are not wet, in a street where every
other person is soaked and water is running off everyone.

HE IS PERFECTLY STILL while everyone around him is moving.

AND HE DOES NOT BLINK. Not once. His eyes stay open and level the entire time.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Documentary, straight on, medium-wide, at eye height. Long lens,
shallow depth — the crowd nearest and furthest are soft, he is sharp. RAIN MUST STREAK, NOT
DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic range like
film — the sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global ambient
fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

Pore-level skin realism on everyone, including him. The crowd are real people — uneven,
ordinary, unposed.

COLOUR: dirty amber, wet grey, brown, oxide. Heavily desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed
blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text or lettering.

A single machine, night, torrential rain, in a flooded street in 2047. No people.

A HEAVY DEMOLITION UNIT BUILT LIKE A BULL. Low, wide, enormously front-heavy, standing in
ankle-deep water facing camera. FOUR SHORT THICK LEGS with a wide stance and blunt wide feet.
Massive forward shoulders, all the mass in the front third, tapering to a narrow rear.

IT IS VISIBLY DAMAGED AND STILL WORKING. ONE SHOULDER IS CRUSHED IN AND HAS BEEN RE-PLATED —
three mismatched plates bolted over the dent in the wrong shade, weld beads unground, so that
shoulder sits lower than the other. It stands crooked because of it.

THE HEAD IS CLEARLY SEPARATE FROM THE SHOULDERS, thrust forward on a short heavy neck and
carried LOW, below shoulder height. IT HANGS SLIGHTLY CROOKED on a neck joint that no longer
centres. A blank battered plate where a face would be, with ONE THIN HORIZONTAL LIGHT LINE
across it, dim and flickering. NO horns, NO eyes, NO mouth.

MATERIAL: bare scored gunmetal and oxide alloy, deeply gouged across the front, rust blooming
from every weld and fixing. Chalked ochre stencils worn to metal. A panel missing from one
flank, exposing dry braided cabling and heavy pistons. Cable looms taped along the outside of
one leg.

IT IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL WITH ITS HEAD DOWN, weight forward on the front legs.

BEHIND IT, A WALL WITH A HOLE PUNCHED THROUGH IT — masonry blown clean out, rubble in the
water, rebar bent outward.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Low camera, wide lens, close, so the shoulders loom. RAIN MUST
STREAK, NOT DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic
range like film — sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global
ambient fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

ALL DAMAGE IS DRY. No fluid, nothing red.

COLOUR: gunmetal, oxide, rust, chalked ochre, dirty amber, wet grey, concrete dust. Heavily
desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text.

Interior location plate. The same large white cyclorama studio, seen from the far end looking
back. Empty plate. No people, no furniture.

THE CAMERA stands at the opposite end at standing eye height, looking back down the length of

The crouched climber rises slowly to his feet on the crown of the machine.

Night. Torrential rain. A vast field of scrapped machinery.

RISING OUT OF IT, ENORMOUS: <<<d8a564fb-13a3-48a8-b89d-68f55d5d0c0e>>> - a mountain of corroded machinery grown
together into one mass, dozens of serpent units fused and rusted into a single body, NINE
MISMATCHED HEADS raised on necks of different lengths and thicknesses. Two of the heads
hang dead and drag. 100% matches the reference. It fills the lower two thirds of the frame
and its full extent runs out of frame on both sides.

ON THE HIGHEST HEAD, VERY SMALL AGAINST IT, A HUMAN FIGURE.

THE FIGURE IS A PURE SILHOUETTE - solid black, no face, no features, no detail of any kind,
lit only from behind. It is a young male shape and nothing more.

THE POSE IS THE ENTIRE IMAGE - CLASSICAL KALIYA MARDANA:
ONE FOOT PLANTED FLAT on the crown of the highest head, weight fully on it.
THE OTHER LEG LIFTED HIGH AND CROSSED IN FRONT, knee bent, foot turned - a dance step, not
a fighting stance.
THE TORSO CURVED IN TRIBHANGA - the three bends, hips one way, chest the other, head the
third. Fluid, relaxed, weightless.
ONE ARM RAISED HIGH ABOVE THE HEAD, holding up a long segmented length of the machine's own
tail, which trails away down behind and disappears into the mass.
THE OTHER ARM EXTENDED OUT AND SLIGHTLY DOWN for balance, hand loose.

THE FIGURE IS NOT STRAINING. NOTHING ABOUT THE POSE IS EFFORT. It is a dance performed on
top of something enormous, and that is what makes it frightening.

THE LIGHT: A SINGLE HARD SEARCHLIGHT BEAM comes down from high behind the figure, from
somewhere out of frame above - an aircraft hunting the field. The beam is a solid visible
shaft in the rain. IT BACKLIGHTS THE FIGURE COMPLETELY, throwing him into total black and
throwing a long hard shadow forward across the machine beneath him. A hard white rim runs
along one shoulder, one arm and the raised leg.

EVERYTHING ELSE IS NEARLY BLACK. The scrap field below is barely readable - shapes,
suggestions, a few dying amber fires far off. The sky is black.

- - - HOW IT IS PHOTOGRAPHED - - -

THIS IS A LIVE-ACTION VFX PLATE, NOT A RENDER.

RAIN MUST STREAK, NOT DOT. Every falling drop is MOTION-BLURRED INTO A SOFT VERTICAL LINE.
The searchlight beam is full of streaking rain. FOREGROUND RAIN CROSSES THE LENS as fast
soft out-of-focus streaks.

THE LENS IS DIRTY AND WET. Two or three water droplets sit ON THE FRONT ELEMENT itself,
soft and out of focus. DIRTY FLARE runs sideways off the searchlight - streaked, coloured,
imperfect, not a clean star.

THE SYMMETRY IS NOT PERFECT. The nine heads are at uneven heights and irregular spacing.
The mass leans. Nothing is centred exactly.

SPECULAR BREAKUP, NOT UNIFORM GLOSS. Wet corroded metal catches light in broken irregular
patches, not an even sheen. Rust is matte where it is thick and shiny only where water
runs.

LOW DYNAMIC RANGE, LIKE FILM, NOT LIKE A RENDER. The searchlight source and the rim on the
figure CLIP TO PURE WHITE. The scrap field, the sky and the underside of the mass fall to
TRUE BLACK with no recoverable detail. NO GLOBAL AMBIENT FILL, NO AMBIENT-OCCLUSION LOOK.

Long lens, compressed, slight atmospheric haze between camera and subject. Focus sits on
the figure; the near foreground and the far field are soft. Vintage uncoated glass, low
micro-contrast, gentle roll-off.

Genuine shadow noise and chroma noise. Visible 35mm-scale grain, coarse and irregular,

COLOUR: black, rust, oxide, wet grey, one hard white beam, faint dying amber in the far

neon.

NO TEXT OR LETTERING ANYWHERE.

POSITIVE LOCKS
The figure is a COMPLETE SILHOUETTE - solid black, no face, no features, no visible detail.
The figure is SMALL relative to the machine - the machine is many times his height.
One foot is planted, the other leg is lifted and crossed in front, knee bent.
The torso is curved in three bends. The pose is a dance, not a fight.
One arm is raised high holding up a length of the machine's tail.

The rain streaks vertically and is visible in the beam.

THE BODY: a colossal braided trunk of dozens of interwoven segmented bodies, thicker than a car, twisting back on itself, with individual strands still readable within the mass. Loose ends of body trail out of it at intervals like severed cable.

THE HEADS: NINE NECKS rise from the mass at different heights and different angles, each ending in an angular armoured sensor head. THEY ARE NOT UNIFORM. Three are large and intact with their armour plates FULLY FLARED into wide cobra hoods. Two are smaller and half-flared. Chalked yellow-grey paint surviving only in patches. Whole armour plates missing, others bent and crumpled. Dry cabling hanging in loops from breaks. FORMAT MODE
Timed multishot, fast cuts. Five shots, four hard cuts at fixed timestamps.

0.0s–1.5s — SHOT 1, THE BILLBOARD
Extreme close-up on the billboard screen, 100mm anamorphic, T2.8, camera holding flat to the glass. A vertical column of dead pixels runs down the middle, a crack spreads across one corner. The panel flickers once. As it does, the camera pulls back fast — a hard dolly-out — the billboard shrinking into the frame as the forecourt and the building behind it come into view.

1.5s HARD CUT

1.5s–3.5s — SHOT 2, WIDE ESTABLISHING
24mm anamorphic, T2.8, low wide, handheld, camera already settled on the full group. Roopa, Nagamma, Helper 1, Helper 2 and Kempa crossing the flooded forecourt right to left, small against the vast lit building behind them. The cracked billboard is small and cheap at screen-left, its cold light raking across the group. The sled trails Roopa on its slack rope, lift units glowing amber. Fog drifts between them and the building.

3.5s HARD CUT

3.5s–6.0s — SHOT 3, THE GAITS
50mm anamorphic, T2.0, lateral tracking at running pace, handheld, jolting with the operator's footfalls. Each body moves differently and naturally: Roopa short and uneven, one arm pressed to her side; Nagamma flat-footed and steady, breathing hard; Helper 1 fast, torch beam swinging; Helper 2 long-strided, bar carried across her body; Kempa in a full double-suspension gallop, ranging ahead and circling back.

6.0s HARD CUT

6.0s–8.0s — SHOT 4, THE DRONES
32mm anamorphic, T2.0, low angle tilted up into black cloud and rain. Two points of light drop out of the cloud. The drones descend fast, level off, and hold station fifteen metres up, rotor wash flattening the rain beneath them into visible spirals. Cut fast to Kempa skidding to a stop in standing water and turning to face them.

8.0s HARD CUT

8.0s–10.0s — SHOT 5, THE STAND
32mm anamorphic, T2.8, low wide, camera behind and below Nagamma looking up past her at the drones. She has already stopped and turned. Roopa and the others continue past her out of frame, still running. Nagamma takes the steel bar from Helper 2's hands without looking at her, plants her feet in the water, and raises it above her head with both hands, facing the drones, holding her ground.
HOLD on this stance. Cut to black.

PHYSICS
Soaked cotton drags with real weight. The sled never touches the ground. Rotor wash disturbs standing water into visible rings and spirals. Rain falls continuously through the full depth of frame in every shot.

LIGHTING
Warm gold at 3200K from the building facade behind, rim-lighting shoulders and wet hair, faces held in soft shadow with detail retained. Hard cool blue-white at 6500K raking in from screen-left off the billboard. Identical light direction and colour across all shots.

COLOR GRADE
Cool and blue overall; warm gold confined to rim light and the building behind. Deep skin tones never lightened. Identical grade across all shots.

AUDIO
Heavy rain on stone and standing water. Distant thunder. Feet moving through water. Breathing. Rotor tone dropping fast from above in shot 4. No dialogue. No music.

STYLE
Photoreal live-action cinematic realism, anamorphic character, monsoon night, fine film grain, handheld, slight grain, shallow depth of field.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
1080p, 21:9, real-time speed throughout, no slow motion in any shot.

POSITIVE LOCKS
No character makes contact with a drone at any point in this sequence. No drone makes contact with any character. Nagamma raises the bar but does not throw or swing it within this shot range. No character leaves the ground. Deep skin tones never lightened. Heavy rain falls in every frame. Cuts happen only at 1.5, 3.5, 6.0, and 8.0 seconds.

A small newborn infant wrapped completely in soft ash-grey cotton cloth, resting on
a flat neutral mid-grey surface.

Proportions: the whole wrapped form is about forty-five centimetres long, roughly the
length of an adult forearm. The head end is large and rounded and takes up about a
quarter of the total length. Below it the form narrows clearly at the neck, swells
outward again to its widest point at the shoulders about a third of the way down, and
tapers steadily to a small rounded foot end. The silhouette is unmistakably a newborn
and never an even cylinder.

The wrapping is hand-wound by someone working quickly, not manufactured. The cloth
overlaps unevenly, one edge sits proud of the one beneath it, and a short loose corner
of fabric hangs free near the shoulder. It is bound with narrower strips of the same
cloth at the chest and below the feet, and the bindings are slightly crooked and drawn
at different tensions. The cotton is worn, nubbed and towelling in texture, damp in
places and darker where it is wet.

It carries real weight. Where it rests on the surface the cloth flattens and spreads
under its own mass and the whole form settles into that contact. The body inside is
lopsided rather than symmetrical — one shoulder sits slightly higher than the other,
and on that side alone a small rounded shape presses outward against the cloth, a knee
or an elbow, stretching the weave taut over it while the other side stays slack.

Where the cotton is damp it becomes very slightly translucent, and beneath it a faint
soft warmth shows through — the diffuse colour of body heat behind wet cloth, with no
edge, no outline and no discernible shape of any kind. Only warmth.

Over the head end sits a compact pale-grey shell curved like a small helmet visor,
covering the head completely with no window, opening or transparent panel. The shell
is old and used: matte, finely scuffed along its crown, with a shallow scratch across
one side and a slightly discoloured repaired seam where it meets the cloth. The cloth
is tucked up under its rim so the two read as one object rather than two. A narrow
horizontal status strip is set into its side, glowing a soft saturated green, with a
small readout beside it.

The wrapping is completely closed at every point. No skin, no face, no hair, no hands
and no feet are visible anywhere, and there is no opening in the cloth.

Hyper-realistic cinematic sci-fi thriller, Bengaluru 2047, torrential monsoon night. Anamorphic widescreen, film grain, IMAX-scale. NO MUSIC — the sound design is the score, and every movement owns one sound. Horror grammar throughout that betrays the audience into tenderness at the very end. Rain haze rations what we are allowed to see; light keeps changing its verdict on her. Five movements:

Movement 1 — THE DEAD WORLD (0–2.5s): Wide, locked frame. The scrap mountain: forty metres of dead machines black against black, rain the only motion. And one sound in the darkness: steel tapping against steel, somewhere up the slope. A pattern. Patient. It has been tapping for years. Hold the frame until the stillness hurts. Then — small, foreground, almost missable — a plate SHIFTS. The tapping stops. The whole mountain seems to listen.

Movement 2 — THE RESURRECTION, IN FRAGMENTS (2.5–6s): Never show her whole. Fragments only, each shot tighter than comfort: a HAND punches up through the plate, fingers articulating one by one, rain streaming off the knuckles — it opens, closes, testing itself after years. CUT: plate sliding off a rising shoulder in sheets. CUT: the bare alloy strut of a leg planting into mud, taking weight, holding. CUT: the back of a head rising into frame, grime sheeting off in the rain. The audience assembles the monster before we ever confirm it. Under this: the grind of settling steel, and up the slope the tapping resumes — FASTER. The mountain is talking about her.

Movement 3 — THE FACE, AND THE LIGHT'S VERDICT (6–9s): She turns toward camera and the light changes its mind about her three times in one slow move: first BACKLIT — a faceless silhouette against the rain haze, pure menace. Then a shaft of side-light as she steps — and half a face: a young woman's, unlined, perfectly intact, serene, beautiful, and deeply wrong in a graveyard. Then full front light as the rain runs the last grime off her — and the truth beneath the jaw: throat and collarbone split open on dry woven filament and bare alloy, nothing inside wet. Beauty above. Machine below. Her eyes wake — not lighting up, WAKING — and they turn, listening to the tapping. She understands what it has been counting all these years.

Movement 4 — THE PILGRIMAGE (9–12s): Low tracking shot, her strut-leg in the foreground ringing one clean metallic note on debris with each even, unhurried step — walking DOWN the mountain toward the collapsed stack of hull plate. Camera precedes her; we arrive at the corrugated steel sheet before she does. Her hand enters frame and moves the sheet aside. Darkness in the gap. A long moment — rain hammering her back — and then, from inside the dark: the GREEN LIGHT, pulsing, painting her face from below. Two heartbeats meet: the tapping up the slope and the beep in the gap, syncing into one rhythm.

Movement 5 — THE ADOPTION (12–15s): She lifts the crate out and opens the lid. THE CAMERA NEVER LOOKS INSIDE. Locked close-up on her face, lit only by the green pulse from below — and the machine face BREAKS: the serene stillness cracks, something floods in behind the eyes — recognition, purpose, something dangerously close to love. A machine discovering what it was made for. Slow push-in and hold. Over it, a man's low, certain voice: "...he would've died before he took his first breath." The green light pulses on her wet face. Cut.

Sound design: no music. Movement 1 — rain and the tapping, then silence when it stops. Movement 2 — grinding steel, the tapping resuming faster. Movement 3 — rain only, close and intimate on her breathless waking. Movement 4 — the single clean ring of the strut per step, then the beep joining. Movement 5 — beep and tapping locked in sync under the voice. The dead world has a heartbeat again.

Critical staging: the four machines are already physically present and walking deep in the shadowed far end of the tunnel from frame one — at first only barely visible: four faint red visor lines bobbing almost imperceptibly with their gait, dull hints of armour catching stray light, the sound of their steps preceding them. Hyper-realistic cinematic sci-fi thriller, Bengaluru 2047, night. Anamorphic widescreen, film grain, IMAX-scale. The collapsed section of a dead tunnel: the ceiling broken open, monsoon water POURING through the breach in heavy columns, one pale shaft of light falling with it into black floodwater. The dead pod drifts and sparks once. NO MUSIC anywhere — the water is the score. The camera is never safe from the water: it sits at the surface, gets splashed, gets submerged — the audience drowns with her. Four movements:

Movement 1 — THE LIFT (0–3s): Water at Roopa's waist and climbing fast. She holds the bundle to her chest, head bowed over it, forehead on the wet cloth, the green pulse glowing between her hands — one breath. Then she inhales and RAISES him — slow motion — the bundle traveling up through the falling shaft of light, water streaming off her arms, until both elbows LOCK dead straight above her head. Camera LOW at the waterline, tilting up: she becomes a pillar in the light. Around her, the black water visibly rises — the shot itself is being flooded from the bottom of frame.

Movement 2 — THE CAMERA DROWNS WITH HER (3–7s): Locked frame, camera half-submerged at the surface — the waterline cuts across the LENS, black water churning in the bottom half of frame, droplets crawling on the glass. She wades straight toward us and the waterline CLIMBS THE FRAME as it climbs her — ribs, chest, shoulders — her face losing territory in the composition inch by inch, the ceiling of the tunnel pressing down the top of frame. The air is running out of the shot itself. Her breathing is ragged, chin tilting up to steal air. INTERCUT one second UNDERWATER: below the surface, looking up — her legs straining against the black, torn kurta billowing, and above, warped through the churning surface, the green light pulsing. Under the surface ALL SOUND DIES to a muffled womb-hush and a slow heartbeat. Back above: the roar returns like a slap.

Movement 3 — THE SUBMERSION (7–11s): She steps and the floor ISN'T THERE. Her head goes UNDER — one violent gasp cut off by black water closing over her face. HOLD THE HORROR: the surface churns where she was — and above it, TWO ARMS remain, locked straight up out of the black water, holding the bundle high, the green heartbeat light pulsing steady in the falling shaft of light. The mother is gone. The hands refuse to go. Hold it — one beat, two, three — the beep the only sound above the muffled deep. Then the water EXPLODES and she ERUPTS back up, gasping, coughing, hair plastered across her face — and the arms never bent. Not a millimetre.

Movement 4 — THE FACE (11–15s): Close, at the waterline with her, water at her throat, her chin up. Push in slow through the rain-fall. Three beats in her face: the animal panic still draining out → eyes closing, half a second that could be surrender → eyes OPEN — and there is no fear in them anymore. None. A resolve that should frighten us. She takes the next step forward into the dark, the green pulse reflected broken on the black water around her face. Hold on her eyes. Cut.

Sound design: no music. Each movement has its own sound: (1) roar of the water column and her breath echoing in the bore; (2) breath and roar above / muffled womb-hush and slow heartbeat below, the switch violent each time the lens crosses the surface; (3) near-silence — just the muffled deep and the bundle's steady beep, then the eruption of her gasp; (4) her breathing slowing to match the beep. The baby's heartbeat is the one sound the water can never cover.

She stands in the pool of cold light, feet planted on the wet concrete, body angled slightly toward the dark tunnel mouth she came from — mid-flight, paused only to listen. water level, the heads above him) and REF B (high angle, the heads closed around him)

SCENE CONTEXT
A tiny figure walks across black water toward a machine the size of a mountain range. The
machine tries to make him stop. It fails. By the end the heads have closed around him on every
side and the camera is looking straight down into the well they have made.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
IT IS NIGHT. Single continuous take, 10 seconds, real-time. The camera performs ONE continuous
move: it opens on the composition of REF A — water level, behind and above the figure, the heads
towering over him — and RISES AND PUSHES FORWARD over his head as he walks, climbing until it
arrives at the composition of REF B, looking almost straight down at him with the heads closed
in a ring. The references are for composition, scale, atmosphere and grade; they are not frames
to be matched pixel for pixel. No cuts, no zoom. Visible film grain. Only diegetic sound. No
dialogue.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
<<<d8a564fb-13a3-48a8-b89d-68f55d5d0c0e>>>: the vast fused mass of corroded segmented machinery with many
mismatched heads on towering columns of ribbed plate, hundreds of metres tall, hoods hinged
open into broad fanned shields, two small hard red sensor points on every head. Rust-bloomed,
water streaming off the plate. 100% matches the reference.
<<<786e8c01-7fc5-4abd-9e92-fd9e6619b01c>>>: an adult man in his twenties, a wide shot seen from far away, tiny on the
water, walking. Lit only from behind by the light above the heads and from below by a band of
dying amber firelight on the water at his feet; base skin tone black, blue only in the rim-lit
highlights. Short wrapped garment, sleeveless vest, barefoot, the flute held loosely in his
right hand at his side. 100% matches the reference.

HIS PACE — this is the whole idea of the shot
He walks at one steady unhurried pace from the first second to the last. Every time the machine
moves at him, his stride does not change, his head does not turn, the flute does not lift. The
camera and the machine do everything; he does one thing.

ACTION
0:00–0:02 Wide, water level, as REF A. He walks toward the heads. The heads are still, angled
 down, red points steady. Rain. The camera begins to rise.
0:02–0:04 THE FEINT. The nearest head on the left DROPS toward him fast — a strike that stops
 two body-lengths short, the hood snapping wider with a crack of plate, water thrown
 off it in a sheet across his path. He walks through the falling water without
 breaking step.
0:04–0:06 THE SECOND FEINT. The right-hand head comes down and across, low, its red points
 sweeping over him and past. A second head behind it rears higher. The columns groan
 and shift. He keeps walking. The camera is now above him, still climbing.
0:06–0:08 THE CLOSING. All the heads lean inward at once from every side, the fanned hoods
 overlapping, the sky narrowing to a slot of pale light above. The camera passes
 over the crown of his head, tilting down.
0:08–0:10 THE WELL. The camera settles high, looking down, as REF B. The heads have closed
 into a ring around him, hoods interlocked, red points in every direction, the amber
 at his feet the only light in the bottom. He is still walking forward into the dark
 at the centre.

PHYSICS AND LIGHT
His pace, posture and the flute never change. The camera move is one continuous physical
crane — real parallax as the columns slide past each other, never a zoom, never a cut. The
heads move with enormous mass: slow to start, fast at the end of the strike, a hard stop
with water shaken off and the whole column swaying after. Rain streaks, never dots — long
smears where the top light catches it; foreground drops cross the lens; two sit on the front
element. Specular breakup on the near plate, none on the far heads. The top light clips to
white and blooms; the red points clip at their cores; everything not lit falls to TRUE BLACK
with no recoverable detail. Coarse irregular 35mm grain heaviest in the haze. The camera
carries a faint drift. This is a live-action VFX plate, not a render. Palette: 60% grey haze
and black water, 30% rust and wet oxide plate, 6% white top light, 3% amber at his feet, 1%
red sensor points. The only blue is the rim highlight on his skin.

AUDIO
Diegetic: rain on metal and on water, the columns groaning as they shift, the crack of the
hood plates locking wider, water sheeting off and hitting the surface, his bare feet in shallow
water — steady, unchanging, four beats to the metre, audible under everything.

armhole notch under each arm. HE IS UNMISTAKABLY CLOTHED FROM THE SHAPE ALONE.

THE FIGURE IS OTHERWISE A DARK SILHOUETTE — lit only from behind, no facial features, no

THE POSE — CLASSICAL DANCING FIGURE:
ONE FOOT PLANTED FLAT on the crown of the highest head, weight fully on it.
THE OTHER LEG LIFTED HIGH AND CROSSED IN FRONT, knee bent, foot turned.
THE TORSO CURVED IN THREE BENDS — hips one way, chest the other, head the third. Fluid,
relaxed, weightless.
ONE ARM RAISED HIGH ABOVE THE HEAD, holding up a long segmented length of the machine's own
tail, which arcs away down behind and disappears into the water.
THE OTHER ARM EXTENDED OUT AND SLIGHTLY DOWN for balance, hand loose.

HE IS NOT STRAINING. Nothing about the pose is effort. It is a dance performed on top of
something enormous.

frame above. The beam is a solid visible shaft in the rain. IT BACKLIGHTS HIM COMPLETELY,
throwing him into near black with a hard white rim along one shoulder, one arm and the raised

THE REFLECTION IS HALF THE IMAGE. The mass, the beam and the tiny figure are all mirrored in

Open water at night over a drowned city. Nothing is happening. Then the sea lifts, and something the

IT IS NIGHT. Single continuous take, 15 seconds, real-time. The camera is LOCKED on a fixed mount low
over the water, roughly two metres above the surface — it does not move, pan, tilt or zoom at any
point. Long lens, compressed. Heavy rain. Visible film grain. Only diegetic sound. No dialogue.

concrete office towers with their lower floors flooded, façade panels missing in patches, windows
blown out, salt bloom and rust running down from every opening; one tower leaning several degrees off
vertical; behind them gantry cranes with their booms still up, cylindrical storage tanks, a pipe rack

THE SCALE — this is the whole idea of the shot
The necks rise to THREE TIMES THE HEIGHT OF THE TALLEST TOWER IN THE SKYLINE. The towers reach only
a third of the way up them. The mass is cropped by the left and right frame edges — it is wider than
the shot. Depth is built with haze: the near necks defined, the far ones dissolving into grey-black
murk. The city, which filled the frame at the start, is ankle-height by the end.

ACTION
0:00–0:04  Locked wide. Black water, low swell, heavy rain on the surface. The drowned skyline sits
           along the horizon, small and still. Nothing moves. Hold.
0:04–0:06  The water between the camera and the city DOMES upward — a broad swelling rise, the
           surface stretching, water running off the top of it.
0:06–0:12  IT BREACHES. The necks come up through the dome one after another, not together, throwing
           enormous sheets of water off the plates as they clear the surface. They rise past the
           smaller structures, past the storage tanks, past the cranes, past the leaning tower, past
           the tallest tower — and keep going. Hoods lock open with a hard crack of plate as they
           clear. Red sensor points come on across the mass. The white-gold crown switches begin to
           blink, high up in the rain.
0:12–0:14  The necks continue up and out of the top of the frame. In the centre, the highest head
           settles and turns down toward the water, hood fully open, and stops — watching. Every
           other head is still rising and moving. That one is still.
0:14–0:15  Water still falling. Hold. Final frame settles here.

PHYSICS AND LIGHT
The camera never moves. The necks have colossal mass — slow to start, heavy through the middle,
water pouring off them in continuous sheets rather than spray. The sea is displaced outward in a low
broad wave that reaches the camera at the end. Rain streaks, never dots — motion-blurred into soft
vertical lines of varying length, falling in gusts and sheets with visibly emptier gaps. Foreground
drops cross the lens as large soft grey smears; two or three sit on the front element, static and out
of focus. Specular breakup, not uniform gloss — some plates sheet with water, others are dry, chalky
and matte. The only light is a diffuse storm glow from above and behind, and lightning inside the
cloud. Everything not hit by it falls to TRUE BLACK with no recoverable detail. Coarse irregular 35mm
grain, heaviest in the shadows. One degree of roll on the mount. This is a live-action VFX plate, not
a render. Palette: 70% black water and wet grey-brown plate, 22% rust and oxide, 5% storm-white,
2% red sensor points, 1% white-gold crown switches. The water is BLACK and the concrete is GREY-BROWN
and rust-stained — no blue and no cyan anywhere in the frame.

Rain on water. Then a deep displacement — the sound of an enormous volume of water being moved, felt
more than heard. The structural groan of plate under load, low and long. Water sheeting off metal and
landing. The hard crack of hood plates locking open, eight times, uneven. Then rain again, and the
low swell reaching the camera. No music.
